pattern.crimePattern: a grandfather poisons the one glass without ice, meant for the young man blackmailing his granddaughter, and his oldest friend, who never takes ice, picks it up first
pattern.notes: Fictional families and house. Teaches REAL TARGET: the woman who died was the one person at the table nobody wanted dead. Oleander is a real, common, poisonous garden shrub; no preparation details beyond "steeped leaves" are given.

ob.reportedBy: Dr. Paul Muriithi, Beatrice Oloo's doctor
ob.text: A doctor reports that his patient, retired diplomat Beatrice Achieng Oloo (63), collapsed and died at her home in Karen on Sunday evening, after lunch at a neighbour's. She had no history of heart disease. He asks for a post-mortem.

facts.text: Beatrice Oloo collapsed and died at home on Sunday evening after lunch at a neighbour's; no heart history.
Dr. Muriithi: no heart history, a normal ECG in May. At 19:00 she called him with nausea, a slow pulse and "seeing yellow". She had lunch at the Carrows'.
Dr. Muriithi: she took no heart medicine and had no allergies.
Her will leaves her house to her nephew, Tobias Oloo.
Joyce: "Ice in every glass, every Sunday. Mama Beatrice never takes ice, so I always keep her glass back and bring it separately."
Joyce: this Sunday Bwana Desmond said "I'll do the tray, Joyce" and carried it out himself at ten to one.
Joyce: when she brought Mama Beatrice's no-ice glass, Beatrice already had one. "I thought, Bwana must have remembered."
Joyce: the young man Marcus invited himself to lunch; Chloe was crying in the kitchen on Saturday night after a call from him.
Joyce: seven people ate the same lunch and nobody else was ill.
Of Sunday's eight glasses, seven carry ice watermarks; one has none, and it carries Beatrice's lipstick.
At the back of the pantry shelf: a small glass jug, rinsed, with a faint green film in the spout.
A patch of the oleander hedge by the kitchen garden is freshly stripped of leaves; the stems still weep sap.
The veranda table: Marcus's chair was at the far end, by the lawn steps.
Records: Chloe paid Marcus KSh 200,000 in four payments since July. Friday, Marcus to Chloe: "One million or the video goes to your university and the police. See you Sunday."
Chloe: on Saturday Marcus said, "Tell your grandfather I'll want my juice without ice." She told her grandfather that night.
Marcus's call log: a 9-minute call 12:46–12:55 on Sunday, taken on the lawn.
In Desmond's outdoor bin: a green-stained sieve and muslin cloth.
In his study: a library book, Garden Plants of East Africa, marked at the page on oleander.
Tobias was at a family wedding in Kisumu from Friday to Monday.
Fingerprints taken from Desmond in detention.
Post-mortem: heart-rhythm failure with no heart disease; passion juice in the stomach.
Post-mortem: death at about 21:30 on Sunday, hours after the poison was taken.
Lab: cardiac glycosides consistent with oleander in her blood, in the no-ice glass's residue, and in the pantry jug's film.
Lab: on the no-ice glass, Beatrice's and Desmond's prints; on the pantry jug, Desmond's only. Nobody else's on either.

Desmond: "Joyce made the drinks. I only carried the tray."
Desmond: "I made nothing special for anyone."
Desmond: "It was meant for that boy. Beatrice took the wrong glass. Beatrice. Of all the people at that table." He asks to see her.
Marcus: "I'm a friend of the family. Chloe and I are on good terms."
Marcus: "It was a business arrangement. She had money, I had a video. Nobody got hurt."
Chloe: "Nobody is blackmailing me."
Chloe: "In June I drove home drunk and hit a parked car. Marcus filmed it. I told Grandpa on Saturday night, all of it. He held my hand and said, 'Leave it with me.'"
Fiona: "I sat beside Beatrice. I didn't see who took which glass."
Tobias: "I inherit her house. I was in Kisumu."

reconstruction.text: In June Chloe drives home drunk and hits a parked car. Marcus, beside her, films it. After they split up he starts demanding money: KSh 200,000 so far. On Friday he asks for a million and invites himself to Sunday lunch.
On Saturday night Chloe tells her grandfather everything, including Marcus's message: he wants his juice "without ice". Desmond holds her hand and says, "Leave it with me."

On Sunday morning Desmond strips leaves from the oleander hedge, steeps them, and strains the liquid into a small jug in the pantry. At 12:50 he says "I'll do the tray, Joyce" and pours one glass of passion juice without ice.

Marcus has stepped onto the lawn for a phone call. Beatrice, arriving late through the hedge, takes the one glass without ice, as she always does. Nobody notices. She goes home at four feeling unwell and dies at half past nine.

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: records on Marcus and a warrant on Desmond's study and bin. The toxicology (18 h) goes with the glass and the jug first thing; detain Desmond after the search, and the prints (6 h) come back inside 24 h.
